newsitem.title: UK: Sumitomo Finance restructures in London.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Finance restructures in London.

text.p: Sumitomo Finance International, the capital markets subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Bank, said on Tuesday that 10 fixed income staff had left the firm in London as part of a refocussing of its fixed income business.
A spokesman for the firm told Reuters the 10 were involved in European government bond trading and sales, where Sumitomo was shifting the emphasis of its business.
"The firm will refocus its fixed income business on JGBs and illiquid bonds. As a result 10 fixed income personnel have left the firm," Sumitomo said in a statement.

Roger Preece, Sumitomo's head of operations, said there would "not be so much emphasis on European government bond trading" and the changes were part of a strategy of "building a strong niche business in core markets". This involved the expansion of the firm's repo business "with additional trading personnel in London and Hong Kong".

Preece said there would also be further people hired to develop the firm's debt capital markets business. This would involve "increasing capacity in both London and Hong Kong, and building up an advanced credit research function concentrating on emerging markets", Sumitomo said.

Sumitomo said it had recently hired 11 senior staff including Bill Donaldson, who is joining its Asian origination team from SBC Warburg, John Kim in Asian credit research who has moved from Bear Stearns and Lee Stowell who is joining its New York sales team from Nomura Securities.
It also said it had made three new hires for its repo team, with the addition of Carolyn Lu from CS First Boston to lead its Asian business.
